record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Can one design a polynomial-time algorithm that PAC-learns the intersection of two halfspaces in R^n? The paper notes this as a major open problem in the context of learning linear threshold structures and convex concepts.

evidence.quote: It is a major open problem to PAC-learn an intersection of two halfspaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer. A halfspace in R^n is a set of the form H = {x ∈ R^n : ⟨w, x⟩ ≥ θ} for some w ∈ R^n and θ ∈ R. The concept class C_2 of intersections of two halfspaces consists of all functions f: R^n → {0,1} of the form f(x) = 1[⟨w_1, x⟩ ≥ θ_1] · 1[⟨w_2, x⟩ ≥ θ_2].

In Valiant's distribution-free PAC learning model, a learner is given access to i.i.d. labeled examples (x, f(x)), where x is drawn from an arbitrary unknown distribution D over R^n and f ∈ C_2 is an unknown target. For inputs ε, δ ∈ (0, 1), the learner must, with probability at least 1 − δ, output a hypothesis h: R^n → {0,1} such that Pr_{x ∼ D}[h(x) ≠ f(x)] ≤ ε.

Question: Does there exist a learning algorithm for the class C_2 of intersections of two halfspaces whose running time (and sample complexity) is bounded by a polynomial in n, 1/ε, and 1/δ, in the distribution-free PAC model?
artifact.status_search_result: Distribution-free PAC learning of the intersection of two halfspaces in polynomial time remains a longstanding open problem. Best-known general algorithms run in quasi-polynomial time, and cryptographic hardness results rule out polynomial-time learning of intersections of n^ε halfspaces under uSVP assumptions, but the case of just two halfspaces is not known to be hard. Recent (2025) work gives polynomial-time algorithms only under restricted assumptions (margin and factorizable distributions).

status_evidence.title: Learning Intersections of Two Margin Halfspaces under Factorizable Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: In the distribution-free setting, learning intersections of two halfspaces in subexponential time is a longstanding open problem; best known algorithms run in quasi-polynomial time d^{O(log 1/γ)}.
status_evidence.claim: Distribution-free polynomial-time PAC learning of intersection of two halfspaces is still open as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: Cryptographic Hardness for Learning Intersections of Halfspaces
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm for PAC learning intersections of n^ε halfspaces would yield a polynomial-time solution to Õ(n^1.5)-uSVP.
status_evidence.claim: Hardness is known for intersections of n^ε halfspaces, but not for just two.
